escalation_condition: Burns covering face, hands, joints, large areas, or charred/white skin
source: ISBI / American Burn Association First Aid
approved_actions: Immediately cool the burn under cool, gentle running tap water for at least 10 to 20 minutes.
Gently remove jewelry, rings, or tight clothing around burned area before swelling starts.
Cover the burn loosely with clean, non-stick sterile gauze or clean plastic cling wrap.
Keep the person comfortably warm to avoid hypothermia while cooling large burns.
Protect blistered areas without disturbing the skin.
critical_actions: Cool with clean water for at least 10 minutes.
Cover loosely with a clean, dry dressing.
contraindications: Never apply ice, ice water, butter, oil, or toothpaste to a burn.
Never pop or puncture burn blisters.
